title: A warm cup before packing up

sections.text: There’s a good minute at the end of camp, when the bedding is rolled and the table is nearly bare. Keep a cup and a flask out for that minute. You can finish a drink without unpacking the kitchen again.

Before the first bag goes in the car, set aside a clean cup, a flask meant for hot drinks and somewhere to pack the used cup. A drink you’ve already made is enough. It doesn’t depend on a stove being allowed, a fire being lit or a tap being in service.

If you haven’t brought a hot drink, have something cold or save the stop for later. Don’t use creek water or an unmarked tap as drinking water. Check the site’s rules and follow any restrictions on stoves and fires.

Set the flask and cup on a level surface away from the edge, out of the path of feet, kids and dogs. A tailgate is handy only if the vehicle is safely parked and nobody needs to load past the drink. Pour when you’re standing still, not with a cup balanced on a knee.

Pour less than you think you’ll want. Leave room at the rim, let the drink cool before sipping and top up only if you want more. The point is to finish it while you’re stopped, not to carry an open hot cup into the driver’s seat.
Save the washing for a sink

Plan to pack the cup out rather than washing it beside water or at a drinking-water tap. Follow posted disposal rules. If there’s no approved place for leftovers or washing-up water, carry them out in a suitable closed container.
Finish the drink you poured. Let the cup cool before putting it away.
Check the table for tea bags, grounds and wrappers. Take them with you, even if they’re compostable.
Pack the used cup separately from clean utensils. Wash and dry it when you reach a proper sink.
Use the cup you already have
